extracted.intended_audience: general readers; students/scholars of comedy, film and television; comedy writers and critics
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and describe the defining features, formats, mechanisms, and exemplar works of the cringe-comedy subgenre for purposes of analysis or creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Cringe comedy is a subgenre of comedy that derives humor from social awkwardness, guilty pleasure, self-deprecation, idiosyncratic humor, and personal distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These listed emotional/social states are the primary raw materials for jokes and scenes in cringe comedy; when evaluating or creating cringe material, check whether the humor emerges from awkward social interactions or characters' discomfort rather than from punchlines or slapstick alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and use of pseudo-reality/mockumentary
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of cringe comedy are pseudo-reality TV shows, sometimes with an air of a mockumentary. They revolve around a serious setting, such as a workplace, to lend the comedy a sense of reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pseudo-realistic framing (e.g., mockumentary style, reality-TV conceit) and placing scenes in earnest/serious settings helps ground the awkwardness; assess whether the form amplifies audience identification and embarrassment through perceived realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protagonist traits: egotism and boundary-crossing
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, the protagonists are egotists who overstep the boundaries of political correctness and break social norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging characters, look for self-centeredness, lack of social filter, or deliberate transgression of norms — traits that create cringe by producing social friction and audience disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism: lack of self-awareness / obliviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: The comedy will attack the protagonist by not letting them become aware of their self-centered view, or by making them oblivious to the ego-deflation that the comedy deals them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core mechanism is that characters fail to realize their own offensive or foolish behavior; evaluate whether scenes preserve the character's ignorance rather than giving them timely self-recognition or corrective consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation (or absence) of moral consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes an unlikable protagonist may not suffer any consequences, which violates people's moral expectations, and also makes the audience cringe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the narrative withholds expected moral correction or punishment; this unresolved moral tension can heighten discomfort and is characteristic of many cringe comedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience response: incongruity versus annoyance (Noël Carroll's account)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cringe comedy relates to incongruity theory and annoyance: some viewers disturbed by deviations from norm will find it annoying rather than amusing; if you find an error genuinely amusing you cannot find it annoying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this distinction to analyze audience reception: determine whether awkwardness produces amused recognition of incongruity or instead pure irritation; the balance between incongruity-based amusement and annoyance helps predict whether a piece functions as cringe comedy for a given audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection to humiliation/comedy-of-humiliation lineage
rubrics_metrics.description: Cringe comedy is linked historically to humiliation comedy (e.g., a key step between Basil Fawlty and characters like David Brent/Michael Scott).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When situating a work, consider lineage and influence from earlier humiliation-focused comedies; evaluate whether the piece emphasizes public embarrassment or the dynamics of humiliating characters in social contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplar works as genre-defining references
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable examples of cringe comedy include films (The 40-Year-Old Virgin; American Pie; Borat; The Lobster; There's Something About Mary; etc.) and television series (The Office; Curb Your Enthusiasm; Fleabag; Peep Show; I Think You Should Leave; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these films and series as benchmarks to compare tone, mechanisms, character types, and audience effect; listing exemplars helps clarify the range of the genre (from broad studio comedies to niche indie or sketch shows).
